gloss: to take at face value; to take seriously; to believe literally

definitions.gloss: to take at face value, to take seriously, to believe literally
definitions.explanation: To accept what someone says as true without questioning or considering that it might be a joke, exaggeration, or sarcasm. Often used as a warning or in a negative context.

examples.japanese: {冗談|じょうだん}を{真|ま}に{受|う}けないで。
{彼|かれ}の{話|はなし}を{真|ま}に{受|う}けてはいけない。
examples.english: You shouldn't take what he says at face value.

examples.japanese: ネットの{情報|じょうほう}を{何|なん}でも{真|ま}に{受|う}けると{危|あぶ}ないよ。
examples.english: It's dangerous to take everything on the internet at face value.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always used with a negative nuance — warning someone not to believe something, or commenting that someone was naive to believe it. Common patterns include {真|ま}に{受|う}けないで (don't take it seriously) and {真|ま}に{受|う}けてはいけない (you mustn't take it at face value).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {冗談|じょうだん}を{真|ま}に{受|う}ける: to take a joke seriously
- {真|ま}に{受|う}けないで: don't take it seriously
- そのまま{真|ま}に{受|う}ける: to take at face value as-is
- {何|なん}でも{真|ま}に{受|う}ける: to believe everything
